chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim, the two sons of Nusayr, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the narrations of Jabir, he said: I never saw him with my father – ever – except for one time, and he never entered upon me [to take Hadith] ever.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the relationship between Jabir and his father regarding hadith narration?
ai.summary: Zurara queries Imam al-Sadiq regarding the authenticity of narrations attributed to Jabir, specifically addressing the chain of transmission. The Imam clarifies that he personally witnessed Jabir with his father, Imam al-Baqir, only once, and that Jabir never entered his presence to narrate directly, suggesting a limited or indirect connection that impacts the reliability of the reports. This highlights the rigorous scrutiny applied by the Imams to the biographical details of narrators in early Shia scholarship.

en.ammaar-muslim: 3. [3/137] Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim the two sons of Nusayr from Muhammad b. Isa from Ali b. al-Hakam from Ibn Bukayr from Zurara who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about the narrations of Jabir, he said: I never saw him with my father – ever – except for one time, and he never entered upon me [to take Hadith] ever.
